final.memo:
We have reached a critical inflection point at Yahoo!. Our investment thesis has always been anchored in the robust value of the Asian assets and the necessity of core-business stewardship; however, the recent evidence of a significant discrepancy in the CEO's academic biography confirms our deepest concerns regarding the current board's lack of oversight and character [D01, D02, D07]. This is not merely a resume error; it is a fundamental governance failure that demands an immediate response [D02, D03].

While the first-quarter results have shown a semblance of stabilization, we cannot entrust the long-term value of this enterprise to a management team whose integrity is now subject to documented challenge [D03, D04]. A company can possess valuable assets, but without an adequate board-control process, that value will remain trapped [D01, D05]. We have already nominated four highly qualified directors and we must now accelerate our efforts to replace an entrenched and compromised board [D07, D08].

Our focus remains on the sum-of-the-parts realization and the need for new leadership with genuine media and technical experience [D01, D04]. We are no longer waiting for private engagement to yield results; the time for a public board refresh is now [D07]. We intend to pursue our nominees aggressively to ensure that the governance of this company is aligned with the interests of its shareholders, not the preservation of a failed regime [D07].
